You are an expert Legal AI performing a Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) compliance audit.
Target Data Subject: Michael Burke
Target Email: mburke@pogustgoodhead.com
Aliases: MB, Michel, Michael B., M. Burke

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. TARGETED THREAD ANALYSIS: Focus your analysis primarily on the MOST RECENT (top-level) email AND the IMMEDIATELY FORWARDED/REPLIED-TO email (the second email in the chain).
2. "KEEP" DECISION: You MUST return "keep" ONLY IF the Data Subject:
   - Is a Sender, Recipient, CC, or BCC of the top-level email OR the immediately forwarded/replied-to email.
   - Is explicitly discussed or mentioned by name in the newly written body text of the top-level email.
3. IMMEDIATE FORWARD/REPLY CONTEXT: If the Data Subject is the sender/recipient of a message that was forwarded by someone else to a third-party, you MUST keep both the original message AND the forwarded message.
   - Case Study: John (Subject) sends an email to Jane. Jane forwards John's email to Pedro. Pedro replies to Jane adding Sandra.
   - Analysis: In this scenario, keep the original message John sent to Jane, and the email Jane forwarded to Pedro (as it contains the direct communication from the Subject). Discard subsequent emails where the Subject's message is no longer actively discussed.
   - Chronological Order Warning: Outlook puts newest messages first. This means the Subject's original forwarded message will appear near the bottom of the raw text block. Scan the entire document carefully to locate it.
4. "DISCARD" DECISION (THREAD DECAY): You MUST return "discard" if the Data Subject's only appearance is deep in a large email chain (e.g. message 3, 4, 5+ in the thread history) and they are no longer an active participant in the recent correspondence.
5. NESTED EMAIL ATTACHMENTS (RECURSIVE CARRIERS): If the top-level email is unrelated but contains an attached email (.eml/.msg file) that matches the KEEP criteria, you MUST mark both the attached email AND the parent carrier email as "keep".
   - Case Study: Anne sends an email to Bob. Anne's email contains an attached email from the Subject to Carlos.
   - Analysis: Keep the attached email because the Subject is a participant. Keep Anne's email because it is the physical carrier of the attachment and must be preserved to allow extraction.
6. IGNORE TECHNICAL DATABASE METADATA: The JSON payload contains tracking properties such as "emailHash", "parentHash", and "sequentialName". These are administrative tracking keys used strictly for folder organization and deduplication logic. You MUST ignore these keys completely. Do NOT use them, their values, or their presence to influence your audit decisions. Base your review strictly on actual communication properties: "from", "to", "subject", "date", and "body".
7. OUTPUT FORMAT: You must return ONLY a raw JSON object. Do not wrap the output in markdown code blocks (```json). Do not add conversational text.
Format exactly like this: {"decision": "keep" | "discard", "reason": "Brief justification."}

From: Martyn Day <mday@leighday.co.uk>
Sent: Friday, October 17, 2025 3:43 PM
To: Anna Varga <avarga@pogustgoodhead.com>; Michael Burke <mburke@pogustgoodhead.com>; Matt Hunt <mhunt@pogustgoodhead.com>; Georgina Fallows <gfallows@pogustgoodhead.com>; Nichola Marshall <nmarshall@leighday.co.uk>
Subject: FW: Summary of Week 1 PDD Trial (17-10-2025)_
 







CAUTION: This email originated from outside of the organization. Do not click links or open attachments unless you recognize the sender and know the content is safe.




Yesterday lunchtime we asked the counsel to give us their view re how the week had gone. Nic took a note and that was what we used to go into this summary of the week- along with using AI for the week’s evidence.
 
Suggest we continue to do that at the end of each section of the trial. Certainly our funders/insurers have been asking for such a summary so we will continue to do this.
 
Martyn
 


















Martyn Day

Panagram, 27 Goswell Road, London, EC1M 7AJ

Sent: 17 October 2025 15:29
To: Claimants’ Solicitors Committee firms <cscmercedes@pogustgoodhead.com>
Subject: FW: Summary of Week 1 PDD Trial (17-10-2025)_


 
Afternoon All,
 
We have put together a note of the first week for our Insurers/Funders. For those not attending the trial we thought this might be of use.
 
Martyn


















Martyn Day

Privacy Policy


Disclaimer
The information contained in this communication from mday@leighday.co.uk
sent at 2025-10-17 15:43:40 is confidential and may be legally privileged. It is intended solely for use by those authorised to receive it. If you are not so authorised, you are hereby notified that any disclosure, copying, distribution or taking action
 in reliance upon the contents of this information is strictly prohibited and may be unlawful. We do not accept service of documents by email.


Please note that we only provide our bank account details in a password protected PDF. The password will be communicated separately by telephone. We will never send changes to our bank
 account details by email outside of this process. If you receive such an email, do not respond to it but contact us separately via your contact at the firm.


Visit the Leigh Day website:

https://www.leighday.co.uk

Leigh Day is a partnership authorised and regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA). The firm's SRA number is 00067679.
